entries.title: RO-Crate 1.3 conformance is asserted but unverified: no validator is obtainable
entries.failed_step: Card §9.1: record the exact validator and its version in every conformance report.
entries.known_fact: §9.1 requires conformance to the pinned base to be validated, and the validator and version recorded.
entries.observed: No RO-Crate validator could be obtained in this environment: `rocrate-validator` is not installable here, and the repository takes no third-party dependencies. All four manifests therefore declare `validator: null`, `validation_result: not_run`, and state the reason in the conformance report itself.
entries.impact: The manifests ASSERT conformance to RO-Crate 1.3 and FTRO v0.0.3 and no tool has checked either claim. Per card §9.1, 'RO-Crate-compatible' means validating against the pinned base; on that definition these manifests are not yet demonstrated to be RO-Crate 1.3. Recorded as unverified rather than presented as conformance.
entries.workaround: None. The claim is marked not_run in every manifest rather than omitted.
entries.proposed_response: Obtain a validator with network access, or write a minimal structural checker for the 1.3 requirements the crates rely on -- accepting that a self-written checker is weaker evidence and must be labelled so.

entries.title: Profile §4 cannot be satisfied in the serialisation §9.1 mandates
entries.failed_step: Attaching the bitemporal quartet to every edge, as §4 requires.
entries.known_fact: §4: every mutable node assertion and EVERY EDGE carries valid_from, valid_to, known_from and known_to. §9.1 pins RO-Crate 1.3, i.e. JSON-LD.
entries.observed: In JSON-LD an edge is a property, and a property cannot carry attributes. Writing the optical and pulsar manifests forced a reified `ftro:Edge` node with edge_class, subject and object -- a class the profile does not declare. The requirement as written is unsatisfiable in the mandated serialisation.
entries.impact: A normative clause that no conforming manifest can satisfy. Found only by writing a manifest, which is precisely why Gate 1 forbids freezing terms first. Both affected manifests use the reified form and are non-conforming against §4 as literally worded.
entries.workaround: Reified ftro:Edge nodes, used consistently and documented.
entries.proposed_response: Profile v0.0.4: declare ftro:Edge and restate §4 in terms of it. Do not amend until all Phase-1 comparison work is complete (card Gate 1).

entries.title: §9.1 mandates a conformance report and declares no node class for it
entries.failed_step: Recording the validator and version in a typed conformance report.
entries.known_fact: §9.1 requires the record; §2 enumerates the node classes.
entries.observed: No ConformanceReport class exists, so all four manifests invented `ftro:ConformanceReport`. Similarly `ftro:time_ephemeris` was needed for the .par's TIMEEPH IF99 declaration, which is neither an ephemeris nor a reference frame.
entries.impact: Two terms the specification requires in substance but does not declare.
entries.workaround: Both used consistently across all four manifests and documented.
entries.proposed_response: Profile v0.0.4, per the vocabulary-pressure report §6.

entries.title: Two thirds of the declared vocabulary has never been exercised against a real product
entries.failed_step: Establishing which profile terms are validated by use.
entries.known_fact: Card §8.1: manifests must be based on real source products, not an abstract ontology exercise.
entries.observed: Across four manifests: 8 of 21 edge classes and 13 of 41 node classes were used. 13 edges and 28 node classes are unexercised. Some are unused because the provider evidence is unresolved (contributes_to, uses_tide_model) -- those are needed. Others simply have no instance in these four legs (analysed_with, transferred_via, ContextualSensorSeries).
entries.impact: Unexercised vocabulary is unvalidated. The profile currently gives no way to tell a term proven against a real product from one that has only ever been written down -- which is the distinction Gate 1's 'nothing is frozen' depends on.
entries.proposed_response: Add an `exercised` marker per term in v0.0.4, populated from this comparison.

entries.title: The profile assumes every domain is a chain; the GNSS leg is only ever consumed
entries.failed_step: Applying one minimum record to a leg that has no ancestry of its own here.
entries.known_fact: §10 states one minimum record set for every dataset, product or evidence manifest.
entries.observed: The GNSS manifest uses ZERO ancestry edges. Its content is pinned artifacts plus two policy objects: within this pilot it is a dependency of other chains, not a chain. Field counts across the four legs are 67 / 64 / 53 / 46, and edge counts 5 / 4 / 1 / 0.
entries.impact: Not an error -- the GNSS manifest is complete for its role. But a leg whose role is to BE consumed plausibly needs a different minimum record from one that consumes, and the profile does not distinguish them.
entries.workaround: None; recorded for the Phase-6 freeze review.
entries.proposed_response: Consider a role-conditioned minimum record in v0.0.4 or later.
